summary: Section 155 of the Companies Act, 2013, stops a person from having more than one official identification number as a director. If you already have this number, you cannot apply for a new one, get another one, or keep a second one. This rule ensures every director has only a single official identification number.
points: Forbids any individual who already has a Director Identification Number from applying for another one.
Forbids individuals from obtaining a second Director Identification Number.
Forbids individuals from possessing more than one Director Identification Number at the same time.
example: Aarav is a businessman in Mumbai who currently serves on the board of Solar Power Solutions Private Limited. He already has a valid Director Identification Number assigned to him under section 154. Later, Aarav forgets his number and thinks he needs a fresh one to join another company, Green Earth Foods Private Limited. He fills out a new application to get a second number. According to section 155, Aarav is not allowed to apply for, obtain, or possess another Director Identification Number because he already has one.

terms.meaning: A unique identification number given to an individual who is a director of a company.

watch: People sometimes mistakenly think they need a new number for every new company they join, but you can only ever have one.
